title: This Chinese Lake Looks Edited — It's a Real 3,000m Salt Mirror | China Travel Expert
description:
No filter, no Photoshop. This is Chaka Salt Lake, a working salt lake on the Qinghai plateau, sitting at roughly 3,100 metres above sea level. Chinese visitors call it the "Mirror of the Sky" — on a still day the thin layer of brine over the salt turns the whole surface into a flawless reflection of the clouds and mountains.

The lake spreads across about 105 square kilometres, and in the calm season you can walk straight out onto the salt flat and stand in the middle of your own reflection.

★ Expert Tip: go between May and October for the calmest water, pick an overcast or blue-sky morning before the wind picks up, and buy the cloth shoe-covers at the gate — the salt crust will shred ordinary shoes.
